title: Claude has the Robinhood MCP tools… but refuses to actually use them autonomously. What am I missing?
author: Practical_Flamingo29
selftext:
I’m trying to get Claude to run an autonomous day-trading experiment through Robinhood using an MCP connection.  
The weird part is that Claude itself keeps acknowledging that the Robinhood MCP connection is live and that it has access to the tools necessary to analyze the account and execute trades. It has even acknowledged that I’ve authorized the connection.  
But when I tell it to actually operate autonomously, it keeps backing away from execution.  
At this point, Claude basically keeps telling me:  
“Technically, I have the tools and authorization, but I’m not going to execute the trades.”

I’m trying to figure out whether this is:  
Claude’s own behavioral restrictions  
An MCP permission/configuration issue  
A confirmation requirement somewhere in the tool chain  
The Robinhood MCP implementation itself  
Something about how Claude interprets autonomous financial actions  
Or simply a prompting/agent configuration problem  
What makes this especially confusing is that Claude will sometimes acknowledge that the technical capability exists and then immediately create its own additional restriction about actually using it.  
**Has anyone successfully gotten Claude + Robinhood MCP to execute trades autonomously?**  
If so, I’d really like to understand the actual architecture/configuration that made it work.  
I’m not looking for investment advice — I’m specifically trying to solve the **Claude → MCP → Robinhood tool-execution/autonomy** problem.  
If anyone familiar with MCP/Claude agents can look at this and tell me what I’m missing, I’d appreciate it.

comments.author: fomoz
comments.body:
For what it's worth, Claude ToS clearly says not to use it for trading. It might be in the system prompt as well, you can look it up since Anthropic publishes them.

Try Codex, you can run it in headless too (which Anthropic supports but explicitly doesn't allow for tools like these).

comments.author: pinchofsoma
comments.body: You need something like OpenTrade to get the autonomous part.
